highlights: Hugging Face moved language model traffic on Inference Providers to OpenRouter, which now selects a provider per call and retries on failure.
vLLM v0.34.0 turns on extensible KV cache by default, removes Model Runner V1, and raises the default block size to 64.
TokenEconomizer, an open-source plugin from UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Microsoft Security, cut coding agent costs by 18.4–30.9% across 277 bug-fixing tasks.

items.title: Hugging Face routes language model inference through OpenRouter
items.summary: Hugging Face switched Inference Providers from its own router to OpenRouter for language model requests, while image, video, and audio generation keep using the existing Hugging Face path. OpenRouter picks a provider per call based on live price, speed and reliability, and retries on another provider if the first one fails, and existing Hugging Face tokens still work. Language model requests are now billed to the Hugging Face account or organization, so custom provider API keys no longer work for them.

evidence.quote: Hugging Face and OpenRouter are teaming up to make open-weight models easy to run.
Today, we are switching Inference Providers from our own custom router to OpenRouter's.

Requests made to language models now go through OpenRouter, which picks the best provider for each call based on live price, speed and reliability, and retries on another provider if the first one fails.
The router supports OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs and Anthropic's Messages API for every chat model, whatever the provider behind it.
Image, video, and audio generation continue to work exactly as before, directly through Hugging Face Inference Providers without going through OpenRouter.
Requests to language models now go through OpenRouter and are billed to your Hugging Face account or organization, so you can no longer use your own API key for a provider with these models.
You can still pick a provider with a suffix on the model id ( model:provider ) or turn providers off in your settings, and your code stays the same.

items.title: vLLM v0.34.0 enables extensible KV cache by default
items.summary: vLLM v0.34.0 sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput, and Model Runner V1 is removed so V2 is the only GPU runner. The release reports up to 1.95× decode on Blackwell and MI355X and 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT. Upgrades need attention: the default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0 is required.

evidence.quote: Extensible KV cache is on by default: vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput.
Model Runner V1 is gone.
Big speedups on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3).
Upgrade check: default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0 is required.

items.title: TokenEconomizer cuts repeated work in AI coding agents
items.summary: TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin from UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Microsoft Security that learns from an agent's past sessions in a repository without modifying the agent or its underlying model. Across 277 SWE-Bench tasks from six repositories, it reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agent and model combinations, while task success rates stayed broadly stable. It runs alongside existing agents, requires no API key of its own, and keeps what it learns on the developer's machine.

evidence.quote: Developers use AI coding agents in the same codebases day after day, yet agents often start each session from scratch: rediscovering familiar facts, loading unused tools, and repeating unsuccessful approaches.
TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model.
Across 277 real bug-fixing tasks, TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents.
Costs fell in every repository tested, while task success rates remained broadly stable.
We evaluated TokenEconomizer on 277 SWE-Bench tasks from six repositories, using five different AI coding agent and model combinations.
TokenEconomizer lowered the average cost by 18.4–30.9%, as shown in Figure 3, and saved the most in all 30 repository-combination pairs without performance loss.
It is designed to run alongside existing AI coding agents without modifying their underlying models, requires no API key of its own, and keeps what it learns on the developer’s machine.

items.title: miHoYo introduces Gamer for long-horizon game interaction
items.summary: The miHoYo Honkai AI R&D team presents Gamer, a generalist Vision-Language-Action foundation model that acts in games through screenshots, keyboard, and mouse. It uses 10K+ hours of gameplay trajectories for continual pre-training and a streaming KV-cache reuse inference engine that the team reports cuts inference latency by over 20× in their benchmark setup. Across multiple main storylines in Honkai: Star Rail, Gamer successfully handles over 95% of the challenges.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments.
We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction.
For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution , and keeps online inference latency low.
We’re excited to introduce Gamer , a generalist Vision-Language-Action foundation model for long-horizon, real-time game interaction, developed by the miHoYo Honkai AI R&D team !
Unlike game-specific agents, Gamer interacts with the world through the same interface humans use: screenshots, keyboard, and mouse .

We leverage 10K+ hours of gameplay trajectories for continual pre-training (CPT) and systematically study scaling laws across model sizes and data mixtures, exploring how generalizable game-playing abilities emerge through scaling.
We develop Streaming-vLLM , a high-concurrency inference engine optimized for continuous game interaction.

Through streaming KV-cache reuse, speculative decoding, and system-level optimizations, we achieve over 20× lower inference latency in our benchmark setup, enabling real-time keyboard and mouse control.
Across multiple main storylines in Honkai: Star Rail , Gamer successfully handles over 95% of the challenges !

items.title: MIRIX-2.0 proposes a multi-agent memory system
items.summary: MIRIX-2.0 is a multi-agent memory system for LLM agents that keeps complete records through six typed memory agents and indexes episodic and semantic records with a provenance hypergraph. It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, leading the strongest baseline by 14.3 points on the latter. It needs no fine-tuning, runs with closed and open models, and its code is public.

evidence.quote: Papers arxiv:2611.12068 Copy markdown MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System Published on Nov 9 · Submitted by Weizhi Zhang on Nov 16 Upvote 47 +39 Authors: Wei-Chieh Huang , Weizhi Zhang , Jiayan Nan , Peng Xia , Yu Wang Abstract MIRIX-2.0 is a multi-agent memory system for LLM agents that achieves h
We present MIRIX-2.0, a multi-agent memory system designed to be practical, accurate, and efficient at once.

It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, where it leads the strongest baseline by 14.3 points, and with AutoDream disabled it gains 31.0 and 22.0 points over HyperMem on single-hop and multi-hop document QA .
Six typed memory agents keep complete records as the system of record, and a provenance hypergraph indexes episodic and semantic records with n-ary frames that cite their rows.
Retrieval runs under explicit budgets, so the evidence a question inspects does not grow with the history.
It needs no fine-tuning , runs with closed and open models , and its code is public.

items.title: V-JEPA-LM reads dynamics from a frozen video encoder
items.summary: V-JEPA-LM joins a frozen V-JEPA world-model encoder to Qwen3 and Llama models, and is trained in a single stage on 4.53M public samples with 32 visual tokens per frame. The resulting 1B to 8B models lead every size class in average score across eleven video benchmarks, and the 4B model scores 72.1 against 61.1 for the best open 4B model. All 6 checkpoints, code and a live demo are open.

evidence.quote: We then build counterfactual supervision that makes the language model read it: pixel transformations turn public videos into answer-balanced variants whose answers are set by the transformation and differ only in the change.

Trained in a single stage on 4.53M public samples with 32 visual tokens per frame , where open video LLMs use several stages, 9M to 172M samples and 64 to 256 tokens per frame on average, the resulting V-JEPA-LM models (1B to 8B, Qwen3 and Llama ) lead every size class in average score across eleven
video benchmarks; our 4B model scores 72.1, against 61.1 for the best open 4B and 64.8 for the best open 8B model.

items.title: Bonbon shows zero-shot capabilities for molecular interactions
items.summary: Bonbon is a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences, without task-specific supervision or structural coordinates. From one representation space it shows zero-shot functional, residue and bond capabilities that generalize to out-of-distribution complexes, and scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters show sharp jumps in every capability at the largest scale. The same frozen representations also achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods.

items.title: Researchers frame agentic robotics and propose an evaluation framework
items.summary: The paper argues that an Embodied System 2, formed by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, is the decision-making core of agentic robotics, where an agent observes, reasons, invokes skills and tools, verifies outcomes and adapts. It proposes an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance, and envisions a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy. The authors note the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap.

evidence.quote: g , Xinchao Wang , Ming Yang , Zhiqin Yang , Zuhao Yang , Tao Yu Abstract Agentic robotics, centered on an Embodied System 2 formed by a foundation model and embodied harness, requires a shared evaluation framework and research roadmap to achieve reliable physical autonomy.
Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks .
It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy.
Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap.
We argue that Embodied System 2 , realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness , forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics .
Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance.

On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy : the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

items.title: VibePrevisBench tests agents on 4D scene reconstruction in Blender
items.summary: VibePrevisBench is a benchmark in which an agent turns a brief into an executable 4D scene in Blender and renders a proxy video, covering 242 tasks across four input kinds. Rule-based Scene Check re-runs the code and compares the exported scene with hidden ground truth facts, while VLM-based Screen Check asks a VLM judge whether those facts are recognizable in the proxy video. Analysis of 11 frontier coding agents found that they inspect their own renders but fail to correct their errors, so item-by-item verification against the brief is still missing.

items.title: MMFlash speeds up speculative decoding for vision-language models
items.summary: MMFlash adaptively upweights visually dependent tokens that the drafter predicts poorly, and uses sparse attention for long video inputs to reduce redundant computation and improve drafting quality. The paper measures token-level visual dependence through the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input, and finds acceptance rates fall from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest. Across various multimodal benchmarks, MMFlash achieves lossless decoding speedups of up to 3.58× and outperforms EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%.

evidence.quote: To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input .
We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training .
Motivated by this observation, we propose MMFlash , a simple and effective framework that adaptively upweights visually dependent tokens that the drafter predicts poorly.
For long video inputs , MMFlash further employs sparse attention to reduce redundant attention computation and improve drafting quality .
Across various multimodal benchmarks , MMFlash achieves lossless decoding speedups of up to 3.58times, outperforming EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%, respectively.

items.title: WebArena-Pro evaluates web agents on self-hosted applications
items.summary: WebArena-Pro is a benchmark of 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications in six domain categories, covering different interface conventions, workflows and data models. The best evaluated results come from Codex with GPT 6.1 Sol and Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 at 62.3%, followed by OpenCode with Kimi 3.1 Pro at 60.7%. Audio and video are treated as core observations alongside text and vision, with dedicated actions for extracting information from each.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.326 adds Code Mode support for agent teams
items.summary: Claude Code v2.1.326 supports turning on Code Mode while agent teams are enabled, so sessions with teams on now start in Code Mode. The release also fixes background sessions losing the LLM gateway exported by the shell, which now stop before any model request, and corrects a misleading "Dangerous rm operation" warning on commands with no rm. It also adds Ctrl+O for hidden startup notices and fixes /rewind restoring only some files after running /branch twice.

evidence.quote: Added support for turning on Code Mode while agent teams are enabled; if you already turned it on, sessions with teams on now start in Code Mode
Fixed a misleading "Dangerous rm operation" warning in the Bash permission prompt on some commands with no rm that Claude Code can't read reliably
Fixed background sessions losing the LLM gateway your shell exported after a crash, after a reopen from another folder, or when the background service lacks it: they now stop before any model request
Fixed /rewind restoring only some files after running /branch twice while a slow backup copy was still running
Fixed /rewind saying "No code changes" when a shell command changed files it can't restore; a turn whose changes weren't tracked now reads "Code changes unknown"

items.title: MEM-SQL reuses historical SQL for text-to-SQL queries
items.summary: MEM-SQL (Memory-EMpowered Text-to-SQL) stores whole-query templates, reusable SQL blocks, and mappings from domain concepts to schema elements, using a layer only when every requirement assigned to it has a match above that layer's threshold. On HARE, a benchmark of 1,600 requests built from 823 verified queries across four datasets, mean execution accuracy across six language models rises from 37.1% for Direct Generation without history to 50.0%. It also uses 76.6% fewer input tokens and 68.8% lower latency on average.

evidence.quote: We introduce HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure the accuracy and cost of adapting historical SQL.
HARE comprises 1,600 requests derived from a fixed pool of 823 verified queries across four datasets.
Our method, MEM-SQL ( Memory-EMpowered Text-to-SQL ), stores whole-query templates , reusable SQL blocks , and mappings from domain concepts to schema elements.
MEM-SQL uses a layer only if every requirement assigned to it has a match above that layer's threshold.
With On-demand Schema Linking (OSL), MEM-SQL consults the schema only when no layer qualifies or the generator judges retrieved evidence insufficient.

Across six language models on HARE , mean execution accuracy rises from 37.1% for Direct Generation without history to 50.0% for MEM-SQL , with 76.6% fewer input tokens and 68.8% lower latency on average.

items.title: OpenAI begins embedded assessments with external evaluators
items.summary: OpenAI begins embedded assessments with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire. The external partners will independently evaluate model alignment, safeguards, and monitoring systems.
